text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment relies on a combination of lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and organ-protection strategies tailored to your specific health profile.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and organ-protection strategies

list.snippet: Nutrition: Focus on whole foods like the Mediterranean diet, high-fiber vegetables, and limited processed sugars.
Physical Activity: Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous aerobic exercise per week plus 2 to 3 sessions of strength training.
Weight Management: Achieving a 5% to 7% (or higher) weight reduction can significantly improve insulin sensitivity and glucose control.
Sleep and Stress: Prioritize 7 to 8 hours of sleep nightly and manage stress through daily movement and recovery habits.

text_blocks.snippet: Current guidelines from organizations like the American Diabetes Association emphasize choosing medications based on your whole health (such as heart or kidney status) rather than just blood sugar numbers alone:

list.snippet: Metformin: Often prescribed as a trusted, low-cost first-line oral pill to improve how your body handles insulin.
SGLT2 Inhibitors (e.g., empagliflozin, dapagliflozin): Pills that help the kidneys remove extra glucose through urine while offering major protective benefits for the heart and kidneys.

GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Dual GIP/GLP-1 RAs (e.g., semaglutide, tirzepatide): Weekly injections that boost insulin release, slow digestion, support substantial weight loss, and protect cardiovascular health.
Other Oral Options: Including DPP-4 inhibitors (gliptins), sulfonylureas, or thiazolidinediones, which may be added or used depending on individual tolerance and target goals.

Insulin Therapy: Considered if blood sugar remains high despite other treatments, or introduced earlier in cases of severe hyperglycemia. Continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) are widely recommended to track real-time levels safely.
